important_evidence: amPEPpy is an open-source, multi-threaded command-line tool for AMP prediction using Random Forest. GitHub: https://github.com/tlawrence3/amPEPpy
panCleave random forest model predicts protease cleavage sites for encrypted AMP discovery; code and data on GitLab (https://gitlab.com/machine-biology-group-public/pancleave).
A benchmark study (PMID 33774670) found amPEPpy to be the best-performing method among >30 tools.
XGBoost model (Bhangu2025) achieved ~87% accuracy and 0.95 AUC-ROC on AMP prediction; trained on 984 AMPs and 984 non-AMPs from amppred server.
Bacteria-specific models for E. coli AMP activity used LASSO/SVM feature selection and SVM/Logistic Regression/Random Forest classifiers.
AMPlify and amPEPpy are mentioned as AI/ML-based AMP prediction tools in a 2025 review on aquatic invertebrate AMPs.
uncertainties: Full text of amPEPpy paper (PMID 33135060) appears to be mismatched in cache; verification needed to confirm dataset, features, and performance details.

No public code or model weights available for the Bacteria-specific (PMID 36912047) and XGBoost (PMID 40529865) models.
Can the E. coli-specific model be generalized to other bacteria, or is it too narrow for a general AMP benchmark?
AMPlify model details were extracted from a review; original paper not yet verified.
